RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-women panel is not evidence of bias — panels reflect who holds senior roles, and women can hire men, just as mixed panels can discriminate. Raising it as your opening point makes you look like you're inferring motive from appearances, which weakens you even if you later find real problems.

Your strong card is the unanswered request. Send a written follow-up, cite the broadcaster's own policy or any applicable access-to-information or equal-treatment duty, and ask specifically: what criteria were scored, what weighting "digital media" carried, and your scores versus the appointee's.

If the reasons come back vague, shifting, or invent criteria not in the advertisement, that's when you have something. Note the panel's composition privately; don't lead with it.
